claimed_purpose.text: Open-source memory system for AI agents combining symbolic short-term memory with layered long-term memory, targeting context bloat and recall failure in long-horizon agents.
Enables agents to manage context across sessions via a four-tier hierarchy
Plugin that injects recalled memories into each turn of conversation

mechanisms.text: Short-term memory offloads full tool logs to external files under refs/*.md and encodes state transitions in Mermaid syntax inside a lightweight task canvas. The agent reasons over the symbol graph; when raw text is needed it greps a node_id to retrieve the file.

L1 memory extraction runs every five turns by default. A user persona is generated every 50 new memories. Recall returns five items by default with a 5-second timeout; on timeout the system skips injection rather than blocking the conversation.

Long-term memory is structured as a four-tier semantic pyramid: L0 Conversation (raw dialogue), L1 Atom (atomic facts), L2 Scenario (scene blocks), L3 Persona (user profile). Upper layers carry structure; lower layers preserve evidence.
Memory assets (Chat Memory, Skills, Wiki, CodeGraph) are bound to agents via Fixed Binding + ACL; permission scope narrows by Team, User, Agent, and visibility before retrieval
Memory is organized into four layers: L0 (conversations/log), L1 (atomic memories), L2 (scenarios), L3 (profiles). L0 is a message log; L1–L3 are curated memory structures.
Memory extraction and aggregation require an LLM; read-only queries may not invoke one, implying LLM-driven extraction is part of the write path from L0 to higher layers.
Isolation dimensions are team, agent, user, and optionally session. The v3 data plane requires all three of team_id, agent_id, user_id; session_id narrows to a session.
Team deletion bypasses the proper Agent cascade by using raw SQL directly against meta_agents, leaving orphaned task_agents, fixed_assets, and chat_memory records
Append-only JSONL (conversation/message log) is explicitly separated from curated memory rows and lives on the others file backend, not the row store
L3 tier builds long-term persona profiles from all past interactions, including behavior patterns, communication styles, and agent-specific rules
Proposed fix: deleteTeams should collect agent_ids first then call deleteAgents() for a full cascade in both sqlite and mongodb adapters
Retrieve path: adapters recall L1/L2/L3 before constructing the next prompt, then inject results as bounded, clearly labeled context.
Checkpoint counters drive L2/L3 pipeline thresholds for persona generation, meaning drifted counts cause premature or missed triggers
Assets follow Team, not individual agent — preventing experience from being trapped in a private account or framework-specific cache
L0 tier persists raw conversation turns including user inputs, agent responses, tool calls, and their outputs as ground truth logs
Memory Proxy injects L2/L3 memory, matched Skills, and knowledge into the system prompt before forwarding upstream on every turn.
Scene index (L2 rows) is derived live from profile rows in rowfs mode; .metadata/scene_index.json is neither read nor written
Auto-recall runs before each turn without the agent explicitly asking; agent can also call tools explicitly to search memory.
When Skills exist, they must be deleted before the Agent is archived, enforcing ordered teardown of Agent-associated state.
The product uses a Gateway and Redis Cluster deployment component, suggesting Redis is part of the memory infrastructure.
recall.scoreThreshold is applied as a single absolute cutoff against retrieval scores, regardless of search strategy
Wiki and CodeGraph assets are not injected wholesale; agents discover them via tools list and call them on demand
Raw conversations are stored as L0 and refined asynchronously through four layers up to L3 persona/profile
Memory content is organized into at least four named layers: L0, L1, L2, and L3, each cleared separately
Session state is deleted (forgotten) on explicit reset — called when a session is /new'd or destroyed.
Forget (clear) is idempotent: re-clearing an already-cleared memory_id succeeds and returns count 0
Ingest at turn time is a no-op on the client; actual ingest is handled by an after_tool_call hook.
Skill mining is handled by an existing MemoryCore component; no new algorithms are introduced here
L0 is a per-day conversation log (full transcript layer), written to a JSONL file keyed by date
A separate index.db is written during ingestion, distinct from the metadata store knowledge.db
New Chat Memory and Skills are private by default; sharing is an explicit action
Remote embeddings are disabled by default; BM25 is the default retrieval method.
Retrieved memories are prepended to each user message as prependContext
Runs on user's own machines; data does not leave local infrastructure

ledger.claim: L0 is a conversation/message log layer; L1–L3 are progressively more curated memory structures (atomic memories, scenarios, profiles).
ledger.quote: **Memory**: L0 conversations, L1 atomic memories, L2 scenarios, and L3 profiles.

ledger.claim: LLM is used for memory extraction and aggregation (the curated write path from raw L0 to L1+), not for read-only retrieval.
ledger.quote: Read-only queries may not invoke an LLM, but memory extraction and aggregation require valid credentials.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Recall is selective (L1/L2/L3), not a full transcript replay; the log (L0) is written but recalled memory is the curated layer injected as labeled context.
ledger.quote: Write completed turns or sessions to L0. Recall L1/L2/L3 before constructing the next prompt. Inject recalled results into the Agent as bounded, clearly labeled context.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Isolation is multi-dimensional: team, agent, user, and optionally session, enforced at the v3 data plane API level.
ledger.quote: The v3 memory data plane requires `team_id`, `agent_id`, and `user_id`. Supply them in the request body or the corresponding `x-tdai-*` headers. `session_id` is optional and narrows operations to a session when provided.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Default retrieval is BM25 (no external embedding service required); embedding-based and hybrid retrieval are available when an embedding API is configured.
ledger.quote: Disables remote embeddings by default and uses BM25 retrieval.
